answer: The juniper multiplier is published, charged in ridge, and fable lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 20 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4349 identities would post 2634 proofs and burn roughly 22 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
